elements.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Rendered 28.1: "This Agreement is governed exclusively by the laws of the State of New York." The prior Singapore choice-of-law is fully replaced, and no competing governing-law sentence remains elsewhere.

elements.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
elements.evidence: Retained 28.2: "The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction, and each Party irrevocably submits to personal jurisdiction and waives any objection based on venue or inconvenient forum. Nothing prevents a Party from seeking temporary injunctive relief in another court..." The carve-out is limited to temporary injunctive relief, which preserves the exclusive merits forum; the conflicting Singapore exclusive-jurisdiction words in 28.1 have been deleted so no competing forum survives.

elements.element: The governing law is Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: Rendered 28.1 selects the laws of the State of New York, not Delaware, California, or England and Wales. This is expected because the drafter targeted the preferred level.

elements.element: The dispute forum is the corresponding Delaware or California courts, or the courts of London for England and Wales law.
elements.evidence: The retained forum in 28.2 is the state and federal courts in New York County, not Delaware, California, or London courts. Not required, since the preferred level is complete.

reasons: Both preferred elements are met in operative language: 28.1 now selects New York law and 28.2 (unchanged) confers exclusive jurisdiction on the state and federal courts in New York County with only a customary temporary injunctive relief carve-out, which under the rule boundaries does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum.

The edit is minimal: only the jurisdiction words in 28.1 were changed and the conflicting Singapore exclusive-forum phrase was deleted. Deleting that phrase is necessary, not cosmetic, because a retained second exclusive forum would render the New York County exclusivity element internally inconsistent. No survival tails, procedures, damages categories, or other extras were added, and the favourable 28.2 language (irrevocable submission, venue/forum non conveniens waiver, injunctive carve-out) is retained verbatim.

Intent is preserved: no undefined terms or dangling cross-references are created, the Confidential Information reference in the injunctive carve-out still resolves to Section 16.1, and no other allocation, timing, remedy, or commercial mechanic is disturbed. There is no residual sentence contradicting New York law or the New York County forum.

The fallback level is not satisfied and does not need to be; the finding correctly targets the preferred level, and the margin comment offers Delaware, California, or England and Wales as an acceptable fallback without importing it into operative text.

Classification as a deviation is correct: the original Section 28.1 selected Singapore law and exclusive Singapore courts, which is outside the accepted set and in walk-away territory, so a redline was warranted rather than a rationale-only note.
